title: Declare quantile-aware request-quality SLI and priority burn controller
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define a set of production-ready SLIs and an operational policy for per-endpoint and per-model request-quality that is quantile-aware and integrates with regional failover and circuit breakers. Deliver a 'priority burn controller' design that adjusts error-budget consumption at runtime using tenant-weight scaling and a sliding-window adaptive burn algorithm. This ticket covers SLI formulas, aggregation windows, alert thresholds, playbook steps for burning/recovery, and the runtime signals required for enforcement (traffic shaping, eviction, model variant fallback).
background: Current SLO efforts focus mostly on latency and availability quantiles and on static error-budget reallocation. Customers running weighted, multi-tenant chat and generation routes have observed quality regressions that are not well-captured by existing SLIs (e.g., increasing hallucination rates at high tail latency or when KV cache misses spike). We need an SLI that jointly captures request-quality (semantic correctness / hallucination proxy), tail latency, and token-completion success, and a policy that can throttle or degrade routes in a priority-aware way without taking down low-latency critical routes.
deliverables: Formal SLI definitions: request_quality_p50/p90/p99, completion_success_rate (per-route, per-model, per-tenant)
Quantile-aware composite SLO declarations (weighted by tenant traffic and business priority)
Design doc for 'priority burn controller' with algorithm, parameters, and integration points
Runtime signals telemetry spec (metrics, tags, and histograms) and example dashboards
Playbook: automated actions for warning/burn/eviction/rollback and manual runbook steps
Test plan and canary rollout with simulations and a synthetic traffic generator
acceptance_criteria: SLI formulas are documented and reviewed by SRE and Applied ML (quality proxies validated)
Controllers implemented in staging that can demo adaptive burn behavior against synthetic overloads
Dashboards show per-endpoint p50/p90/p99 request_quality and composite burn-rate across regions
Circuit breaker integration: when composite burn > threshold, failover and eviction decisions are triggered according to policy
Runbook created and approved; oncall knows how to escalate and how to perform emergency burn cap adjustments
Automated tests for sliding-window controller validate bounded oscillation and respect tenant weight limits
implementation_steps: 1) Define request_quality SLI: combine hallucination-proxy score (via eval prompt), token_completion_rate, and tail latency into a normalized 0..1 metric
2) Choose quantiles and windows: p50/p90/p99 with 1m/5m/1h aggregation windows for different signal uses
3) Design composite SLO declaration format (json schema) with tenant weight, route priority, and regional preferences
4) Prototype sliding-window priority burn controller in staging (python service) that consumes SLI streams and outputs per-route burn-rate commands
5) Implement enforcement hooks: routing policy changes, model-variant fallback, and soft-eviction (queue backpressure + early exit tokens)
6) Integrate with existing circuit-breaker service: map burn thresholds to breaker states and regional failover triggers
7) Add telemetry: new metrics, histograms, and traces; wire dashboards and alert rules
8) Run chaos/synthetic tests: inject latency, KV-miss bursts, and degraded model outputs to validate controller responses
9) Iterate on tuning parameters and publish the playbook; schedule a follow-up retrospective after the canary rollout
risks: Quality proxy (hallucination detector) may produce false positives under distribution shift
Controller oscillation can cause thrashing between eviction and restore if windowing is misconfigured
Incorrect tenant weight scaling could starve low-priority customers or over-protect noisy tenants
Operational complexity: more state to maintain across regions increases debugging overhead
Rollback path must be safe; mistaken global evictions could impact enterprise customers
notes: Prefers using histogram-percentile aggregation in Prometheus where possible; use reservoir sampling for high-cardinality tags
We will store sliding-window controller state in durable per-region Redis with TTLs to survive restarts
Start with conservative default tenant weights: {"enterprise": "0.6", "startup": "0.3", "free": "0.1"} and expose tunable via Console
Plan to pair this rollout with model-variant fallback capacity (cheaper quantized variants) to preserve availability while reducing cost
